articles.title: SpaceX merge with Tesla is on the Horizon
articles.content:
This Newsletter is called AI Supremacy and so part of my mission to consider various possibilities in the future of AI. But what if the future of Space-technology1 and AI are linked? And of recent increasing relevance, are the politics of Elon Musk even compatible with the stories of the future he is known for? Is the aging Tycoon still investible? 2 I’m looking for diverse opinions on this:
Lately I’ve been thinking about the merger of SpaceX and Tesla, which seems like it’s 95% going to happen soon. There are apparently “committees” at both Tesla and SpaceX looking into the merger. In recent years I’ve become a lot more interested in space-technology and in recent months more interested in National Defense with the Iran and Ukraine conflicts both seemingly escalating. When it came out that Elon Musk ordered Starlink to be throttled (speed restriction) for Ukraine, it got me a bit concerned.
Musk said on SpaceX's earnings call that the two companies have formed committees of independent directors to explore the possibility of a deal.
On the SpaceX Earnings call he basically said Tuesday that he would like to see the consolidation of his business empire by formally merging his two largest companies, SpaceX and Tesla. We know that consolidation is quickly approaching, either in 2027 or 2028 itself.
Elon Musk already has unprecedented control over SpaceX shares and owns about one fifth of Tesla. A combined entity is an incredible concentration risk, where Tesla continues to build inside of China. If SpaceX and Tesla combined it would be in the area of a corporation with a market cap of around $3.5 Trillion dollars. To put things in perspective that’s about equal to the GDP of France.
Elon Musk has a few big projects that could benefit from having a more diversified company with Tesla:
Scale Starlink
Dramatically increase launch cadence of Starship
Scaling own AI chips: Terafab
Winning the race to Orbital Compute (Datacenters in space)
Scaling Energy to compete with China
Winning the robotics and Physical AI race
Contributing to founding a sustainable Lunar Base (and colony)
Colonizing Mars, and contributing to making civilization multi-planetary to increase our chances for survival
With a bigger company, and one that he has more full control over, Elon Musk would be able to do a huge amount of M&A to ramp up SpaceX into a fairly large monopoly on the frontier of the Space economy, robotics, AI and AI compute infrastructure.
Tesla: Musk holds approximately 15% to 20% of equity (around 20% including vested options).
SpaceX: Musk holds approximately 40% to 42% of economic equity, but maintains over 80% voting power due to SpaceX’s super-voting Class B share structure.
So if you do the math, Musk would alone control in the area around 35% to 42% of total economic equity in the combined company with far higher voting rights.
Elon Musk could do significant M&A in semiconductors, aerospace, space-connectivity, and even National Defense, acquiring someone like Andruil, advanced manufacturing companies (e.g., Hadrian) and Physical AI software brain companies for humanoids. The stock share leverage of a combined entity of SpaceX and Tesla would give the company a lot of optionality and Musk would be able to dominate the future of Space.
How do you call a company a monopoly when it’s at the frontier of many rather high-risk and speculative emerging technology projects? SpaceX could also be scaled into National Defense entity that becomes weaponized for a kind of peculiar world domination for an oligarch class. Starlink has been incredible implicated in politics and geopolitics. Whatever the legacy of Elon Musk, this entity is likely going to be his last chance.
Tesla brings manufacturing scale, Energy, batteries, EVs, and robotics to the table. SpaceX brings launch dominance in rockets, a struggling xAI business that got stronger with Cursor3, Starlink global connectivity4, aerospace engineering with more shared projects like AI chips via Terafab. Is the combined entity better positioned to achieve what Elon Musk hopes to achieve? It would appear so. The combined entity would be better positioned for the large capex required and aggressive M&A that would be needed.
Tesla in 2026 will spend around $20 Billion in Capex, while SpaceX will likely do around $65 Billion. That’s $85 Billion of Capex just in 2026. Tesla has around $16 Billion of debt, SpaceX have closer to $40 Billion of debt. There’s no guarantee this would work out. SpaceX becoming profitable by being a Neo Cloud is not a great sign for its long-term financial sustainability.
A merger of Tesla with SpaceX was always part of the plan obviously for Elon Musk:
“Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussions,” he said, but he added that “I think it would be a good idea.”
Elon Musk sees himself as a visionary and a combined entity gives him a longer career to explore that vision. If the AI bubble pops there will be a lot of interesting AI startups, Physical AI, Inference AI chip and semiconductor companies on sale, that SpaceX could acquire.
In harsher times, SpaceX could cherry pick bleeding AI, aerospace and space-technology startups while attracting more talent to its side with more financial leverage.
Elon Musk is part of a group of Silicon Valley tycoons who believe the era of energy abundance, superintelligence and multi-planet human capability is right around the corner. They believe having more agents and robots than people is a good idea, that will lead to a better life where off-world infrastructure enobles us on Earth5.
SpaceX, Tesla and all of Musk’s companies already share talent, have circular vendor financing and investments, share major infrastructure projects, that can be bundled into Musk’s evolving grand vision for the future of humanity.
For instance one of the new promises is that SpaceX is positioning orbital data centers (powered by abundant solar energy in space) as a major future revenue source and one of the keys to dominate the future of AI and compute. Given how poorly Tesla handled its robotaxi promises it will be interesting to see if the combined entity can fulfil any, some, or all of these grand projects, dreams and promises.
Now that SpaceX went public with the largest initial public offering on record - the combined entity would have a fairly diversified business model that could super-charge even grander ambitions. Albeit perhaps, with a limited real-world actual impact on consumers and civilization.
Bundling and merging Tesla into SpaceX also enables the company to hide some of its less than stellar aspects into yet another hype cycle. Tesla’s Q3 Earnings were not good where operating income plunged 56% year-over-year to $718 million as operating expenses jumped 39%. Deliveries and automotive revenue were both down.
SpaceX will require stupendous R&D, gigantic Capex6 and nearly flawless execution to pan out in accordance with the words of Elon Musk. That’s highly improbable. But doing massive and aggressive M&A might be the only way to keep the story alive, and a combined entity can do that much more efficiently than keeping the companies separate.
SpaceX began trading on the NASDAQ exchange in New York City at $135 a share, valuing SpaceX at nearly $1.8 trillion. The stock is now trading around $146. Tesla still somehow has a market cap of $1.5 trillion and while it’s not great for shareholders to combine the entities, it will happen. Elon Musk is the most consequential paper Trillionaire on the planet.
Production of Optimus humanoid robots has started on high-volume lines in Fremont and SpaceX’s AI business is hopefully just getting started. Starship being fully reusable and ramping up cadence opens up more possibilities for Space, aerospace and National Defense supremacy.
The merger will face scrutiny by US regulators but doing it (rushing it) while Trump is still POTUS is the goal. SpaceX also in recent months said they will build a massive new $100 billion spaceport named Starbase, in Louisiana in Vermilion Parish along the Louisiana Gulf Coast.
Tesla has a Forward P/E of 182, and SpaceX has an equally aspirational market valuation. Musk’s only hope is to do a massive Space-tech roll-up and spend big on compute and hope it pans out. But if you are investing in the combined entity, you are essentially investing in Elon Musk and the power of American capital, against all odds, including China. Musk’s politics is also a significant business risk, as recently he has committed roughly $366 million to the 2026 midterm election, with much of it aimed at preserving or expanding Republican power in Washington. But at 55, some of Musk’s magic and perhaps his sanity has declined. A projection of an almost childlike masculinity7 and transcendental con.
Those are big rockets you have sir. I hear you want to build a lot of robots. But the majority of Elon Musk’s vision remains highly speculative, with timelines that rarely match up with reality. Tesla makes 85% of its revenue from selling electric vehicles. It’s a car manufacturer pretending to be something more even after all these years. SpaceX makes the vast majority of its revenue from Starlink and selling compute as a Neo Cloud. It could take the combined entity easily a decade to take a meaningful step closer to its vision. As Tesla Robotaxis have demonstrated, that vision can also come a decade late, or not at all.
Some call Musk a genius, a visionary, a technological fraud or a corrupt tycoon, but the future is self-interested. SpaceX will still have to fight for its survival. The combined Tesla and SpaceX entity could have some serious geopolitical, China8 and Succession issues and challenges ahead9.
Orbital compute in Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO), could fundamentally alter and radically change the relationships between the future of AI and Space-technology companies.
Elon Musk is a figure whose legacy is deeply complex, polarising, and far from invisible. A hero to some, a villain to others and a path that China has and will likely supplant.
Only after a $60 Billion Acquisition. Not earned.
Starlink that has long been considered the key revenue growth driver of the company pre 2027.
Many are starting to question the human benefits and social value of Elon Musk’s companies and future vision.
The Space Neo Cloud, the original SNC, a weird convergence of low-earth-orbit infrastructure and dirty datacenters.
With significant characteristics of Asperger's syndrome and interpersonal narcissism with seemingly limited capabilities for empathy.
Tesla relies heavily on China for manufacturing (Giga Shanghai) and market demand. Conversely, SpaceX is a key U.S. defense contractor deeply integrated with national security, launch systems, and military communications. These conflicts of interest make Elon Musk unreliable.
Where Elon Musk owning too many SpaceX shares means that its biggest problem will be Elon Musk, and also what happens to the company after he is gone.
President Donald Trump awarded Elon Musk the National Medal of Science on October 8, 2026, during the “Science: A New Golden Age Summit”. The National Medal of Science is the highest honor the United States bestows in science and engineering. Elon Musk has been a major donor where during the 2024 presidential election cycle, Elon Musk spent roughly $250 million to $290 million specifically backing Donald Trump's campaign including using his ownership of Twitter/X for Trump’s campaigns. On X, Musk posted or reposted hundreds of messages in support of Trump to his 200+ million followers, generating tens of billions of views.
Ahead of Germany's federal elections, Musk openly endorsed the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), declaring that "only the AfD can save Germany".
European officials explicitly labeled Musk's posts and platform changes as a form of foreign political interference. His abuses of power include interference in the political processes of Brazil, France, United Kingdom and other countries.
Elon Musk’s Starlink Ukraine and Department of Government Efficiency (DODGE) interference are significant dents in his global reputation and beyond the scope of this article. His increasing geopolitical controversies, challenges facing his core business ventures and polarizing conduct add to the already considerable concentration risk of whatever SpaceX becomes.
Whether you are a fan or a critic of Musk, he’s putting oligarchs front and center with regards to the power that will come with technological progress in the 21st human century of history. SpaceX is as much an experiment in Moon shots as it is a diversifying company with perceived value mostly based on Elon Musk’s own reputation.

articles.title: Grok Bot Tutorial: How to Build an AI Team That Works Without You 24/7
articles.content:
Good Morning,
Yesterday Anthropic announced weeks before their IPO, Claude Duet - a professional partner you can trust.
It’s basically their answer to Grok Bot, the topic of our hands-on guide (see more guides here) today by (AI Blew My Mind). Duet is a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent. It comes to you with what needs your attention, completes tasks you ask of it, keeps working when you step away, and checks with you before it acts on your behalf.
For instance for businesses, entrepreneurs, managers, executives or small business owners imagine: Duet can delivers a daily briefing and handles tasks ranging from scheduling meetings to building financial forecasts and web apps. Duet is for professionals, and thus feels polished and specialized.
The target customer audience for Claude Duet is most similar with the audience of Cursor’s Grok Bot. See the promo video.
Professionals of all kinds have to juggle many decisions a day, and Anthropic designed Claude Duet to be the most useful. Duet is built around Anthropic’s Opus 5.5 model and is initially available to US subscribers on Pro and Max plans, sharing existing usage limits. Most of our upcoming guides (this month) have to do with these Personal productivity agents.
For me Duet looks the most promising for small business owners and entrepreneurs. As to be expected, Duet integrates with over 6,000 connectors in the Claude Marketplace, including Gmail and Slack, and can make purchases via Stripe's Link digital wallet and Shopify's Shop pay. Claude Duet is in Research Preview and will roll-out slowly. It was announced on October 21st, 2026.
helps you turn decades of experiences into AI systems that work 24/7 for you, so you don’t have to. She’s for me the perfect ambassador to break down how to use these productivity boosting tools.
Jev AI Blew My Mind: 15 Ways to Use It Without Code
Claude Dashboards Tutorial: Turn Messy Business Data Into Dashboards That Update Themselves
How to use NotebookLM with Claude Code: 5 demos + 50 use cases with prompts
I asked Daria to give my readers an easy to absorb guide to Grok Bot. The more I look into these personal agents, the more they seem like productivity focused tools.
Cursor made Grok Bot’s growth is part of the reason SpaceX just released surprisingly decent Earnings. Grok Bot as of early October, 2026 has in the area of 800,000 paid weekly users. Cursor was acquired by SpaceX for $60 Billion. I was always very bullish about the talent at Cursor. Watching how Anthropic Duet and Grok Bot evolve is going to be interesting if you believe AI is going to boost personal productivity in meaningful ways at work, for entrepreneurship and for where a lot of Americans actually work, in small businesses across a range of diverse industries.
So, let’s get into the guide.
For the past few years, using AI meant having a conversation. You asked, it answered, and then you took the answer somewhere else and did the work yourself.
At the start of this year, OpenClaw went viral for taking over that last step. It was an AI agent that did the work itself, using the apps on your computer, and it kept going even while you slept.
But to get it running, you had to work in a terminal, set up API keys and know how to configure and secure it yourself, often on a Mac mini bought just to keep it on day and night. So for all the excitement, it stayed a tool for technical people.
That barrier didn’t last long. Once people saw what an agent could do for one person, every big AI company raced to build a version anyone could use, and the results arrived within months.
Grok Bot launched in August, Meta released Muse in September, OpenAI followed with ChatGPT Dots a few weeks later, and Google announced its Gemini agent for businesses in October.
And now, the future OpenClaw gave us a glimpse of is just one download away, ready to take on any kind of work for you, without a Mac mini in sight.
The one I’ve spent the most time with is Grok Bot, and it’s the one we’ll dive into today.
The Cursor team, now part of SpaceX, gave me early access a couple of weeks before it launched, and I was really impressed by how well it all works and how easy it is to get started, even if you’re not technical at all.
So in this guide, I’ll show you how to set up Grok Bot, build your first bot step by step with the exact prompt behind my morning briefing, and grow it into a team of AI employees that passes work from one bot to the next.
What Grok Bot is and how it works
Grok Bot vs Claude and ChatGPT
How to set up Grok Bot
Build your first bot: a morning briefing, step by step
Turn your bots into a team with group chats and a team lead
What to lock down before you hand over the keys
Grok Bot works like a messaging app for your team, except every teammate is an AI. You hire a bot for each job you want done, and when new work comes up, you hire another.
Behind the chats, all your bots share one computer in the cloud, with a browser, files and the logins you’ve saved. That’s what lets them use your tools, sign in to websites and click through them the way you would, and keep working after you close the app or shut your laptop.
And since everything lives in the cloud, your team goes wherever you go. You can check in, hand out new tasks and approve their work from the desktop app (Mac or Windows) or from your phone.
Bots (your AI employees): each one has a name, a job title and a job description, just like a new hire. The clearer the job description, the better they work, and we’ll write one together below.
Group chats (your team meetings): put a few bots in one chat and they work together. One finishes a task and hands it to the next, the way a colleague passes you a file and says “your turn”.
Routines (their daily schedule): tell a bot when to work, like “every weekday at 7am”, or what should get it moving, like a new email or a new Slack message. Then it gets to work on its own.
Connect Apps (the keys to your tools): this is where you give your team access to Gmail, your calendar, Slack, Notion, Google Drive and the rest. You’ll also find ready-made bots here that you can hire as they are.
Approvals (your sign-off): you choose what needs your OK first, like sending an email or paying for something. The bot does the work and waits for your yes.
Primary bot (your team lead): the one bot you mark with a star. It keeps an eye on everything and offers to take on new work before you even ask.
If you already use Claude or ChatGPT, you might wonder whether your AI assistant could do all of this too. It can, and I run two systems like this myself: an interactive one I work in every day, and an automated one where agents run my business workflows and I only step in to approve.
But getting there takes a bit more effort. You need to know how to design a system like that, write its instructions, set up its memory and carefully plan every workflow you want it to run, then keep it all working.
Grok Bot and the other personal agents that launched this year do most of that work for you, so you can start with one bot today and build from there.
Since October 12, Grok Bot comes with The X Subscription, which bundles Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor and X Premium into one plan. Grok Bot starts on Premium.
If you already pay for SuperGrok or Cursor, you can keep your current plan. Before you upgrade, know two things. First, X doesn’t say exactly how much you can do on each plan, only that each one gives you more usage than the one below it. Second, upgrading merges your X, Grok and Cursor accounts into one, and you can’t separate them again.
Before you hire your first bot, let’s get everything ready for your new team. You only do this once.
Download the desktop app (Mac or Windows) from x.ai/bot and the Grok Bot app on your phone. The phone app is where you’ll approve actions and read what your bots did, so it’s worth setting up on day one.
Once the app is installed, open Connect Apps in the sidebar. This is where your bots get access to the tools you already use.
Search for the tools you use, like Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, Notion and Google Drive, and click Add next to each one. It takes you to sign in to that account, and once you do, Grok Bot can use it. And you can connect more than one account to the same app, which is a lifesaver if, for example, you juggle several inboxes.
Or skip it for now. When you ask a bot to do something with an app you haven’t connected yet, like “summarize my inbox”, it shows you how to connect it right there in the chat. In the screenshot below, you can see how I connected both of my Gmail inboxes simply by talking to the bot.
In the same Connect Apps section, click Bot templates to open the Marketplace, full of bots other people have built for everything from sales and marketing to recruiting and your personal life.
Scroll through it, pick the ones that could be useful to you and add them.
They’re ready to go as soon as you connect the apps they need, so you get a head start and see how bots work before you build your own.

On October 16, 2026, China's Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and the Ministry of Science and Technology published a joint draft document proposing significant updates to the country’s export control catalog. The policy update places 23 AI-related technologies under formal export restrictions, expanding government oversight over overseas transfers of model weights, source code, agentic frameworks, and specialized compute clusters.

The distinction could allow Chinese AI developers such as DeepSeek ​and Alibaba to continue expanding internationally while giving Beijing greater oversight of transfers of sensitive ⁠AI technology abroad.

U.S. Fears China, Bans DeepSeek

The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) issued a formal order directing all federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek software, applications, and third-party tools incorporating its models from government IT systems. The order, originally issued on July 24, applies to federal civilian agencies, including the Treasury, State and Justice departments, but it excludes the Department of Defense.

Amazon and Google Announce Important CUDA like Software updates for their ASICs

Amazon announced TorchNeuron as a free, open-source tool aimed at bridging PyTorch code directly to its custom Trainium and Inferentia AI chips. Rather than requiring developers to manually adapt custom CUDA operators or rewrite software stacks for AWS silicon, TorchNeuron enables execution via simple configuration changes.

Google introduced TorchTPU, targeting seamless PyTorch integration across its Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) infrastructure. TorchTPU acts as a translation and compilation layer that hooks PyTorch execution directly into Google’s custom compiler and TPU hardware backends. They could foster more widespread adoption of TPUs and Trainium chips.

But will they truly hurt CUDA’s moat? PyTorch is the popular open source toolkit that AI app developers and startups use to build, train, and run AI models. In 2022, Meta turned PyTorch over to the Linux Foundation, a nonprofit that manages many important open source projects. Google says it worked directly with Meta, Hugging Face, Inferact (maker of vLLM), RadixArk (maker of SGLang), and others to ensure that TorchTPU’s features and code libraries work well with these popular AI development tools, just as the original PyTorch does. Google’s TPU AI chip business has the most to gain.

Anthropic S1 Leak Details Spook Confidence just 3 weeks from IPO

OpenAI acquires biotech startup

Orchestra Bio is a startup building AI agents to help pharmaceutical companies manage drug development. Orchestra Bio's team and agent technology are being integrated directly into Rosalind, OpenAI’s life-sciences platform. Part of OpenAI’s recent marketing insists it can transform the future of science. However I must say, OpenAI’s M&A strategy and history is not sparkling. OpenAI’s talent for copycat moves continues as the deal draws direct comparisons to Anthropic's acquisition of Coefficient Bio, which closed for a reported approximate $400 million in stock.

Cracks are appearing in America’s debt-laden $10tn AI infrastructure boom as project delays

When too much Capex, is still not enough.

Geopolitics, rising bond yields and macro stories are disrupting the AI story. The Trump Administration has broken the Capex thesis. Let’s try and go into a bit more detail on that angle.

AI Projected Shortfall in Compute is going to be Massive

According to JPMorgan, global AI compute demand is expected to reach roughly 530 GW by 2031, while available supply is projected to reach just 250 GW. That leaves us with a staggering 280 GW shortfall, even after the industry spends hundreds of billions of dollars expanding capacity.

The software, silicon (GPU) and model cycles are moving faster and faster relative to Physical AI Infra, datacenter, energy and HBM bottlenecks.

This shortage forces a radical over-spend where rising bond yields leads to an eventual crash. At least, that’s my base case thesis.

The Big Ask, Circular Financing and Borrowed Money

The AI boom is increasingly being built on borrowed money. As you might have anticipated, AI-related bond issuance has surged to $419 billion so far in 2026, 90% higher than all of 2025. We might be near a tipping point likely in 2027.

The Infinite Demand Thesis is Beginning to Crash

Corporate token spending growth collapsed from 42% in July to 0.2% in September, per Ramp data. Meanwhile, return on invested capital at the five biggest hyperscalers fell from 38% to 20% as capex outruns earnings.

There are structural signs that ROIC is actually declining.

The Pressure of Growth that doesn’t translate to ROIC is Mounting by the Quarter (2026 squeeze begins)

Cost of tokens rapidly declining while most of adoption are from agentic swarms that aren’t translating into real Enterprise adoption that’s sustainable.

Elon Musk’s Ukraine Abuse of Power

Elon Musk ordered the slowdown of a version of SpaceX's Starlink that Ukraine has relied on in its war against Russia, The Wall Street Journal reported.

Musk and President Donald Trump discussed the move to throttle Starlink "soon after" the change first became public last week. Both are aging poorly in a world where they will soon lose their power. How do you rectify the bloated SpaceX market cap with such an abuse of power in a conflict zone? Paying for Starlink now has a moral dilemma.

The move made both the Trump Administration and Elon Musk brands less popular further decreasing AI sentiment among already bearish consumers. The move led to widespread confusion and an internal scramble across Washington with U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stated the Pentagon issued no formal directives to limit the network, noting that SpaceX makes independent decisions regarding its terms of service. With boths sides denying responsibility where Musk has considerable business in Russia allied China.

Supply-Demand Shortage for BigTech will only Increase

Iran Conflict Becoming Regional Sends Brent Crude Higher This Week

Dark Semi Nights

In Mid October, 2026 Semiconductor Stocks have now traded red for 8 straight days, their longest losing streak in 16 years.

When Capital Can’t move or solve the AI Demand Blight

Morgan Stanley now sees $1.6 trillion in total 2027 capex. More is never enough when it comes to AI. Where many major firms are cutting back on closed-model token spend per employee in mid to late 2026.

Donald Trump Administration Accelerate U.S. Debt and Interest Payments

Over the last 10 years, US Federal Government Tax Revenue has increased 65% to $5.4 Trillion while Government Spending has increased 92% to $7.4 Trillion. The result: a more than doubling of the US National Debt from $19.8 trillion to $40.4 trillion. Most Americans aren’t even aware of this.

What Would Collapse of Social Order Even Look like?

France can’t afford its own deficit. Now it’s also picking up a €1.2 billion riot damages bill. Debt at 119% of GDP. Rates already surging. No currency of its own to inflate away the problem.

What will be the social cost of an AI Inflation led affordability crisis? Just ask France. With mounting corruption in the U.S. in Government, the crisis begins to spill over to the AI trade as consumers shun AI products, slop and work pressure.

AI isn’t just Inflationary, it’s going to be Sexist

That is, Women may be at greater risk of AI job losses. The history of technological progress suggests that, as AI spreads, the employment impact will hit women more than men. Recent data and labor analyses—including reports from the International Labour Organization (ILO)—highlight that women face a statistically higher exposure to generative AI job disruption than men. So sad to say that women face higher risks from generative AI in 88% of analyzed countries.

Datacenter Delays and Moratorium Compound Losses

At least 47 major data center projects have been DELAYED, withdrawn or blocked so far in 2026. Grassroots resistance has escalated into a national (U.S.) movement. More than 1,000 U.S. communities have sought restrictions, zoning bans, or temporary moratoriums on AI infrastructure.

Furthermore, Industry analysts (such as those at Bernstein) have cautioned that only roughly 35% of the total planned U.S. data center pipeline is currently considered credible or realistic given the harsh realities of supply chain bottlenecks, transformer shortages, and liquid-cooling constraints. Huge wastages of capital at the model (duplication) and capex (Infra) levels.

French Riots Spread to Milan as Bond Yields Spike

France's 10-Year Bond Yield just hit its highest closing level in more than 22 years. French riots over affordability (even pre austerity) have now spread to Italy, Spain, Portugal and even Belgium. In Spain it’s housing, and in Portugal it’s over rising rents.

Rental Rates on even Older Nvidia GPUs are Rising Fast

This is boosting the cost of compute and inflating the cost of Capital Expenditures. Even as HBM shortages continue. High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) shortages (SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron) are not only still ongoing, but they remain one of the primary binding bottlenecks across the entire AI hardware supply chain.

Bond Yields Rage as Protests Rock Europe

10-Year Real Yield hits highest level since the Global Financial Crisis . ⏰

Neo Cloud Debt to Equity Sends Warning Signals

SpaceX Revenue Diversifies Substantially

Token Prices Fall as Agent Swarms Take Over

Over the last year, the effective price per one million (1 Mil) AI tokens has fallen by more than 50%. The AI slop internet is about to get an even more automated quality.

Why Open-Weight Models are Winning

Tokens are flowing to different models depending on task, cost, and efficiency. Harnesses and routers mean open-source models have more pricing power for a majority of tasks.

Is China Winning in Open-Weight AI Supremacy?

The 2027 to 2028 period might be the key years.

Europe is Over-Spending on Physical AI and Spuculative AI Startups

Europe in its desperation to keep up with the U.S. and China are now spending in a Venture Capital sense too much, too late, in the AI cycle. It’s what they should have been doing in 2024 and 2025. For instance:

  9. Universal Quantum 🇬🇧: $100M. Modular quantum computing systems.

  10. Breye Therapeutics ApS 🇩🇰: $77M. A Copenhagen biotech.

  11. eleQtron 🇩🇪: $66M. Quantum computing.

  12. RougeTx 🇳🇱: $58M. The first treatment for HHT, a rare blood vessel disorder.

  13. Biorce 🇪🇸: $51M. AI to accelerate clinical trials.

  14. Isembard 🇬🇧: $50M. AI-powered factories for aerospace and defence manufacturing.

  15. Sensible Biotechnologies 🇬🇧: $47M. mRNA produced by engineered cells.

  16. constellr 🇩🇪: $43M. Thermal satellite imaging.

While Europe has some leverage in emerging technologies like Physical AI and Quantum, it’s general AI positioning is not good.

AI’s Impact on Academia and Science is Alarming

It’s not just about Mathematicians. According to the Economist, Scientists adopting AI appear to be finding success. Yet, while a boon for individuals, a study shows AI use shrunk the range of topics studied and cut scientists’ engagement with each other’s work.

More AI Races Emerge in the pressure for AI Supremacy

Energy Infrastructure and Russian Oil Crisis

Ukrainian strikes have knocked out more than 45% of Russia's oil refining capacity in recent escalating weeks. On the other hand, Russia’s strategy focuses on destroying electrical generation, transmission nodes, thermal plants, and natural gas storage to disrupt civilian life, degrade war industries, and induce severe winter heating crises. The Ukraine and Middle East conflicts appear to be escalating.

Open-Weight Models are Changing the Future

Wikipedia was written in volunteer hours. This AI age commons is written in GPU-hours and data. With Nvidia acquiring HuggingFace, your marketing is my marketing. In effect, Meta, NVIDIA, Alibaba, DeepSeek, Moonshot, Mistral and about ~30 other labs have shared close to $1B (!) worth of training compute on the Hugging Face hub. All of it free to download. At the end of 2023 that number was under $40M.

Will the Personal Agent Fad even Last?

We are about to be bombarded by AI devices and AI personal agents. Forbes just dropped its first-ever Agentic 20. Who do they feature? So you think you are a Personal agent adopter? Try these:

  • -> Instinct - personal assistant living in iMessage. $10B valuation, 14 people, $1B in annual transactions.

  • -> Meta Muse - the finance-fixing agent. 5M downloads in 3 weeks.

  • -> Fo by Wajo AI - books your plumber, humans step in when it gets stuck.

  • -> Pion by Andon Labs - agents running a real store, a café, and 4 radio stations.

  • -> Known - AI matchmaker. 60% of intros accepted.

  • -> Town - AI coworker for small teams. $50-200/user, 9x growth since July.

  • -> Govra - AI tax auditors for governments. Already piloting with California.

  • -> Dots by OpenAI - always-on agents, connect to 4,000+ apps.

  • -> Hermes by Nous Research - open-source agents Fortune 500s run on their own servers.

  • -> Atarraya - AI running shrimp farms in shipping containers. $22M raised.

  • -> Viktor - the “AI employee” you hand a revenue target. $50M ARR in under 7 months.

  • -> TeamTangoAI - answering calls for funeral homes.

  • -> Grok Bot by SpaceXAI - teams of agents working in parallel. 400K weekly users.

  • -> Link by Stripe - payment layer for agents. Agentic purchases up 38x in a month.

  • -> Browserbase - the browser agents actually use. 2,000+ years of browsing automated.

  • -> Exa - the search engine built for agents. $250M raised, $2.2B valuation.

  • -> XBOW - AI red teamers. 14,000+ exploits found in real apps.

  • -> Element451 - AI admissions agents. 400+ colleges on the platform.

  • -> Salient - AI agents for loan servicing. $40M ARR.

  • -> Stuut - agents chasing invoices. $3B moved through the platform.

Weird AI Devices set to take over Holidays Soon

Amazon last week introduced Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse, two wacky looking AI devices.

  • Bee is “personal AI” that remembers what matters from your conversations and turns it into useful insights and reminders.

  • Bee Frontier is Amazon’s so-called next-generation “AI wearable”, and Bee Eclipse is a magnetic phone attachment.

  • Of course you can also connect Bee to Alexa+ to ask Alexa for hands-free summaries and to-dos, or to Amazon.com for personalized shopping.

  • Bee is private—audio is processed in real time then deleted, and customers have control of their data.

Bee Frontier is $74.99. Bee Eclipse is $99.99. Frontier comes in Onyx, Lavender, and Sage. While Eclipse comes in Silver, Midnight, Honey, and Blush colors. Apple is of course releasing its own suite of Apple Home Collection products. AI devices are essentially always-on by default, for the privacy conscious be warned.

According to OpenRouter Data

Open-weight models took 72% of tokens and 27% of spend last week, in the 2nd week of October, 2026. If they continue to take more token marketshare could begin to erode some of OpenAI and Anthropic’s margins. OpenAI weight gaining token marketshare over closed-weight models is one of the biggest stories of 2026.

Anthropic’s Characterization of RSI

While OpenAI used the “AGI” marketing trick, it appears “RSI” is the prefered acronym for Anthropic. Anthropic employees using Claude Code and the model itself doing more of Anthropic’s R&D work is supposed to be some sort of ramp to RSI. Real superintelligence would imply RSI generalized to everything and independently developing outside the scope of human oversight and organization. An AI singularity for which there is no empirical evidence for.

Nvidia’s Cadence of Nemotron is showing Rapid Improvement

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL achieves twice the intelligence of its predecessor, Nemotron 3 Super (13), and does so using ~60% fewer output tokens per task. It launches alongside Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, the first model in its new Bolt family, which scores 21 on the Intelligence Index by Artificial Analysis. Nvidia routinely ships smaller revisions or specialized checkpoints every 2 to 3 months between major updates that took about 5.5 months (170 days). Together that’s the cadence of a potential frontier model maker of the future for open-source.

Just a few days later, DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, a minor yet high-performance update to its DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model family.

New Kind of Visual Model called Glimpse

I’m bullish on one new approach to multi-modal LLMs. For former Google DeepMind researcher and Elorian CEO Andrew Dai this is a step towards more visual reasoning. Mid-reasoning, it can crop into a region, pull specific frames from a video, or run code to measure or compare what it’s looking at, a mechanism Elorian calls a “visual scratch space.” Think of someone pinching to zoom on a phone photo to double-check what they thought they saw. It was announced about five days ago.

Read More about It

The Rising Productivity Gap

McKinsey's 2026 state of AI survey, published in August, found that 80% of respondents say AI has improved their personal productivity, while 37% say it has contributed to EBIT, essentially unchanged from last year.

A recent HBR article offers an interesting perspective on that gap: many companies are using AI to automate individual tasks while leaving the broader processes around them largely unchanged. You can hire more forward deployed engineers (FDEs) but there are structural issues to this adoption story. You need to completely redesign workflows and roles to see max gains. That is, nearly 75% of companies generating the strongest returns from AI are fundamentally redesigning their workflows, compared with roughly 20% of other organizations. This means the impact of AI is a culture story so much as it’s a tech story. Still that’s not the same as real labor productivity data in society at large.

There was so much more I had wanted to cover, but all of these are just snapshots in the end.

I’ve run out of space and time, three days of work and curation. Hope it illuminated.

Mike

ChatGPT in recent months have added so many more options with Codex, ChatGPT Work and other new additions. OpenAI claims Dots are always-on AI agents integrated into the ChatGPT ecosystem. I asked to give us a simple but detailed guide to OpenAI’s AI agents called Dots.

Claude Code for Beginners: The Complete Course in One Post

OpenAI introduced dots on their lats OpenAI DevDay about two weeks ago. This is the guide by of the Newsletter LearnAIWithMe.
“Unlike Codex or ChatGPT, Dots are meant to operate independent of any specific hardware or interface, pursuing user-defined goals continuously in the background with minimal oversight.”
OpenAI released Dots on September 29, and I’ve been testing it ever since.
OpenAI introduced Dots on September 29, powered by GPT-6 Astra.
Now let’s jump straight in.
To reach Dots, you need a ChatGPT Pro plan.
Pro comes in three usage tiers: $100, $200, and $500.
All three include Dots. I’m on the first one.
The rollout is gradual, so it can take a few days to show up in your account. If you can’t find it, open chatgpt.com/dots.
After you upgrade your account, click on “Your dot” and then “Continue”.
Step 1. Open Your dot and click Continue.
Next, it asks you to connect your apps to make it more helpful.
Step 2. Dots asks to connect your apps. You can skip it.
Since I don’t have any annoying meetings on my calendar, I clicked on “Continue without connecting additional plugins.”
Next, it started setting up my Dot and asked me to wait a couple of minutes.
Step 3. Setting up your Dot takes a couple of minutes.
I feel like I bought a new Apple product and am setting it up. At this step, it asked me to choose where my Dot can work.
It even has its own cloud computer, so it can keep working while I’m away from my laptop.
But I also wanted it to read my files, so I selected it like this below.
Step 4. Choose where your Dot can work and what it can read.
It wants me to customize it, and it answers me in both Turkish and English because I talk to it in two languages.
Your Dot answers in the languages you already use with it.
I clicked on “Customize your dot”.
Step 5. Click Customize your dot.
I named my Dot after my favorite TV show character, with a little adjustment.
(Burhan Altintop + Alfred the butler = Alfred Altintop)
And I picked the following “characters” and “pets”, and clicked on “Save”.
Pick a character and a pet, then save. Mine is Alfred Altintop.
When I clicked his name:
Click your Dot’s name to open its page.
This page opens.
Here I can call him, connect with him via Slack, and see his tasks.
Your Dot’s page. Call it, connect on Slack, see its tasks.
Being able to call it is a really powerful feature.
Dots are very similar to OpenClaw, Hermes, or Grok bots, but being able to call your Dot is a huge differentiator.
Here is the conversation.
Your Dot doesn’t live only inside ChatGPT. You can connect it to Slack.
To do that, I clicked the Slack icon here:
Step 1. Click the Slack button on your Dot’s profile.
Next, it asks for my approval. I clicked on “Add to Slack”.
Step 2. Pick your workspace and click Add to Slack.
After a few seconds, it connects. Then click Open Slack.
Step 3. Connected. Click Open Slack.
And here it is, ready on Slack.
Alfred’s first message on Slack.
You can now talk to it on Slack. Add it to a channel, mention it, and it answers in the thread, like this.
Mention your Dot in a channel, and it replies in the thread.
You can check your Slack connection from here.
Alfred’s profile. Slack sits right next to Call.
It’s the same Dot with the same memory. Moving from ChatGPT to Slack doesn’t reset anything.
One gotcha. Adding your Dot to a channel doesn’t mean it watches that channel. To make it monitor, tell it which channels to check, what to watch for, and when to ping you. Then ask it to confirm the recurring task.
My favorite idea from OpenAI’s own docs.
Keep routine progress in ChatGPT, and send only the decisions to Slack.
(If your Slack belongs to a company workspace, your admin has to turn Dots on first.)
I reviewed X to see what people actually do with Dots. Here are four that show something real.
Now let’s say you feel lazy, but you still have things to get done.
First thing, open your computer and give your Dot access to it. (Open your Dot’s profile, find your computer under Computers, and click Allow access.)
Then you can leave the desk.
OpenAI shows exactly this in the video below.
A message goes out from the phone, and since the computer is still on, the Dot gets Codex working on it.
Video by @ChatGPT on X.
In this example, one message asks for three things, and the Dot splits it into three Codex tasks and writes the instructions itself.
A few minutes later, the phone buzzes, telling you all PRs are ready to review without even sitting at a computer.
Now let’s say you want to run a whole company with Dots.
First thing, connect your apps and set your approval rules up front.
(What your Dot can do on its own, and what has to wait for you.)
Then you can stay a team of one.
@beamnxw drew exactly this in the video below.
One founder sits on top, and one Dot runs the work around them.
Video by @beamnxw on X.
In this example, one Dot runs five workstreams for sales, operations, content, research, and product.
In the end, it puts you in the loop, so you approve everything, which is the most important thing.
Now let’s say you want a trading bot, but you don’t want one AI deciding alone.
First thing, give each model one job. (One writes the agent, one brings the data, one checks it.)
Then you can let three models do the work.
@Sprytixl shared his setup in the video below
Video by @Sprytixl on X.
In this example, this guy built a trading bot using Jev, Sonnet 5.5, and OpenAI Dots, and he says it backtested 1,840 trades over four years in one hour.
Sonnet 5.5 writes the agent, Dots bring the data and 240 test cases, and Jev fences it and ships it. The build took 55 minutes and $4.92, and 221 of the 240 tests passed.
But one thing to tell you. I did the same thing in this post, and OpenAI Dots can’t make trading decisions. I believe that’s why he added Sonnet 5.5 to the mix.
Now let’s say your inbox is a mess, but you don’t want to open it.
First thing, connect your email to your Dot. (In your Dot’s profile, go to Customize and then Plugins.)
Then you can just ask.
Thibault Sottiaux from OpenAI showed exactly this in the video below.
His tip is to ask your Dot to “create a pet and set it as your avatar,” so his Dot even has its own face.
Video by @thsottiaux on X.
In this example, one question asks how many unread emails he has, and the Dot answers 39,939, with 21,498 in the inbox.
01-thsottiaux-dot-pet.mp4
Right after, it offers to sort out what actually needs his attention first, without him even opening the inbox.
I’ve been using Alfred for two weeks now.
If I had to compare it with OpenClaw or Hermes Agents, which I think are the closest alternatives, being able to call it and let it use your computer whenever you want is a big plus.
But is it worth the $100 subscription? If you don’t use it for anything else, I don’t think so.
Thanks for reading.

“Unlike Codex or ChatGPT, Dots are meant to operate independent of any specific hardware or interface, pursuing user-defined goals continuously in the background with minimal oversight.”

OpenAI Dots

I tested it for two weeks. Here is the setup, the Slack connection, and 4 use cases worth copying.

OpenAI released Dots on September 29, and I’ve been testing it ever since.

OpenAI introduced Dots on September 29, powered by GPT-6 Astra.

Now let’s jump straight in.

Dots

To reach Dots, you need a ChatGPT Pro plan.

Pro comes in three usage tiers: $100, $200, and $500.

All three include Dots. I’m on the first one.

The rollout is gradual, so it can take a few days to show up in your account. If you can’t find it, open chatgpt.com/dots.

How to Create OpenAI Dots?

After you upgrade your account, click on “Your dot” and then “Continue”.

Step 1. Open Your dot and click Continue.

Next, it asks you to connect your apps to make it more helpful.

Step 2. Dots asks to connect your apps. You can skip it.

Since I don’t have any annoying meetings on my calendar, I clicked on “Continue without connecting additional plugins.”

Next, it started setting up my Dot and asked me to wait a couple of minutes.

Step 3. Setting up your Dot takes a couple of minutes.

I feel like I bought a new Apple product and am setting it up. At this step, it asked me to choose where my Dot can work.

It even has its own cloud computer, so it can keep working while I’m away from my laptop.

But I also wanted it to read my files, so I selected it like this below.

Step 4. Choose where your Dot can work and what it can read.

It wants me to customize it, and it answers me in both Turkish and English because I talk to it in two languages.

Your Dot answers in the languages you already use with it.

I clicked on “Customize your dot”.

Step 5. Click Customize your dot.

I named my Dot after my favorite TV show character, with a little adjustment.

(Burhan Altintop + Alfred the butler = Alfred Altintop)

And I picked the following “characters” and “pets”, and clicked on “Save”.

Pick a character and a pet, then save. Mine is Alfred Altintop.

When I clicked his name:

Click your Dot’s name to open its page.

This page opens.

Here I can call him, connect with him via Slack, and see his tasks.

Your Dot’s page. Call it, connect on Slack, see its tasks.

Being able to call it is a really powerful feature.

Dots are very similar to OpenClaw, Hermes, or Grok bots, but being able to call your Dot is a huge differentiator.

Here is the conversation.

Dots on Slack

Your Dot doesn’t live only inside ChatGPT. You can connect it to Slack.

To do that, I clicked the Slack icon here:

Step 1. Click the Slack button on your Dot’s profile.

Next, it asks for my approval. I clicked on “Add to Slack”.

Step 2. Pick your workspace and click Add to Slack.

After a few seconds, it connects. Then click Open Slack.

Step 3. Connected. Click Open Slack.

And here it is, ready on Slack.

Alfred’s first message on Slack.

You can now talk to it on Slack. Add it to a channel, mention it, and it answers in the thread, like this.

Mention your Dot in a channel, and it replies in the thread.

You can check your Slack connection from here.

Alfred’s profile. Slack sits right next to Call.

It’s the same Dot with the same memory. Moving from ChatGPT to Slack doesn’t reset anything.

One gotcha. Adding your Dot to a channel doesn’t mean it watches that channel. To make it monitor, tell it which channels to check, what to watch for, and when to ping you. Then ask it to confirm the recurring task.

My favorite idea from OpenAI’s own docs.

Keep routine progress in ChatGPT, and send only the decisions to Slack.

(If your Slack belongs to a company workspace, your admin has to turn Dots on first.)

Dots Use Cases

I reviewed X to see what people actually do with Dots. Here are four that show something real.

1- Your Dot runs Codex for you

Now let’s say you feel lazy, but you still have things to get done.

First thing, open your computer and give your Dot access to it. (Open your Dot’s profile, find your computer under Computers, and click Allow access.)

Then you can leave the desk.

OpenAI shows exactly this in the video below.

A message goes out from the phone, and since the computer is still on, the Dot gets Codex working on it.

Video by @ChatGPT on X.

In this example, one message asks for three things, and the Dot splits it into three Codex tasks and writes the instructions itself.

A few minutes later, the phone buzzes, telling you all PRs are ready to review without even sitting at a computer.

2- Your Dot runs a one-person company

Now let’s say you want to run a whole company with Dots.

First thing, connect your apps and set your approval rules up front.

(What your Dot can do on its own, and what has to wait for you.)

Then you can stay a team of one.

@beamnxw drew exactly this in the video below.

One founder sits on top, and one Dot runs the work around them.

Video by @beamnxw on X.

In this example, one Dot runs five workstreams for sales, operations, content, research, and product.

In the end, it puts you in the loop, so you approve everything, which is the most important thing.

3- A trading bot with Sonnet, Dots and Jev

Now let’s say you want a trading bot, but you don’t want one AI deciding alone.

First thing, give each model one job. (One writes the agent, one brings the data, one checks it.)

Then you can let three models do the work.

@Sprytixl shared his setup in the video below

Video by @Sprytixl on X.

In this example, this guy built a trading bot using Jev, Sonnet 5.5, and OpenAI Dots, and he says it backtested 1,840 trades over four years in one hour.

Sonnet 5.5 writes the agent, Dots bring the data and 240 test cases, and Jev fences it and ships it. The build took 55 minutes and $4.92, and 221 of the 240 tests passed.

But one thing to tell you. I did the same thing in this post, and OpenAI Dots can’t make trading decisions. I believe that’s why he added Sonnet 5.5 to the mix.

4- Your Dot checks your inbox

Now let’s say your inbox is a mess, but you don’t want to open it.

First thing, connect your email to your Dot. (In your Dot’s profile, go to Customize and then Plugins.)

Then you can just ask.

Thibault Sottiaux from OpenAI showed exactly this in the video below.

His tip is to ask your Dot to “create a pet and set it as your avatar,” so his Dot even has its own face.

Video by @thsottiaux on X.

In this example, one question asks how many unread emails he has, and the Dot answers 39,939, with 21,498 in the inbox.

01-thsottiaux-dot-pet.mp4

Right after, it offers to sort out what actually needs his attention first, without him even opening the inbox.

Final Thoughts

I’ve been using Alfred for two weeks now.

If I had to compare it with OpenClaw or Hermes Agents, which I think are the closest alternatives, being able to call it and let it use your computer whenever you want is a big plus.

But is it worth the $100 subscription? If you don’t use it for anything else, I don’t think so.
